h1: The 6 Best Halloween String Lights of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Halloween String Lights: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Halloween string lights under $25, scored on run length, linking, lighting modes and weatherproofing.
summary: The weillsnow 500 LED string is the one to buy for sheer coverage, running 164 feet on low-voltage power. The DAZZLE BRIGHT 300 LED set is the better pick for a mid-size porch, because up to three strings link together. The 20FT 100Ct purple and orange set suits railings and trees, and the Runleo pumpkin string is the battery-powered choice for mantels where there is no outlet. Every set here costs under $25.
intro: Most Halloween string light disappointments come down to one number printed on the box and ignored: how many strings can you plug end to end. Buy a 100-light strand, connect a second, then a third, and the plug quietly overloads or the far end goes dim. Before you pick colors or modes, find the connection limit and match it to the length you actually need.

We ranked six Halloween string light sets, every one under $25, by reviewing their listings for run length, connection limits, lighting modes, power type and weatherproofing. Coverage per dollar carries weight because these sets are cheap, but we also scored whether a set can run outdoors in rain and whether it remembers its last mode after you switch it off.

products.name: weillsnow 500 LED Halloween Lights Outdoor, 164 FT Twinkle Lights Waterproof
products.verdict: Five hundred orange and purple LEDs across 164 feet, waterproof and low voltage.
products.description:
The weillsnow set strings 500 LEDs over 164 feet in orange and purple, runs on 29 volt low-voltage power, offers 8 modes with memory and is listed as waterproof fairy lights. Low voltage is the quiet advantage: it runs cooler and is safer around damp outdoor wiring than a mains-voltage strand.

It tops the list because nothing else here covers as much distance. The DAZZLE BRIGHT stops at 300 LEDs per set, and the 20FT set at 100, so for a roofline, a fence or a big tree the weillsnow needs the fewest strands and plugs. It remains under $25 despite that length.

Buy it for whole-house outlining or a big yard display. The caveat is that 164 feet of thin wire tangles quickly in storage, so wind it on a cardboard reel, and a long run needs an outdoor outlet within reach of the power adapter.
products.idealFor: Rooflines, fences and large trees that need maximum run length.
products.skipIf: You only need to dress a small porch or mantel.

products.name: DAZZLE BRIGHT Halloween 300 LED String Lights
products.verdict: A 300 LED set with 8 modes that links up to three strings together.
products.description:
DAZZLE BRIGHT sells a 300 LED Halloween string with 8 light modes and the ability to connect up to three strings, with the listing noting a total below 1000 LEDs. That stated connection limit is rare in this price class and is the number to trust, because it tells you how far you can chain sets before the plug overloads.

It ranks second because the weillsnow covers more distance in one strand. Where DAZZLE BRIGHT wins is flexibility: you can buy one set for a porch and add two more for a bigger display, instead of committing to 164 feet from day one.

Buy it for a mid-size porch and entry, with room to expand next year. The caveat is that the summary does not state waterproofing, so check the listing for outdoor use before hanging it in rain, and keep connections off wet ground.
products.idealFor: Porches and entries that may grow into a larger display over time.
products.skipIf: You need the longest single run in one strand.

products.name: 20FT 100Ct Purple Orange Halloween Lights for Outdoor Indoor Decorations
products.verdict: A 20 foot, 100-count purple and orange set that is UL certified and end-to-end connectable.
products.description:
This set is a 20 foot string of 100 purple and orange incandescent lights, end-to-end connectable and UL certified. Incandescent bulbs give a warmer, more traditional glow than LEDs, which many people prefer for pumpkin-and-witch lighting, and UL certification is a useful signal for anything plugged in outdoors.

It ranks third because 20 feet is short next to the weillsnow, and incandescent bulbs draw more power and run hotter than LEDs. Against the Joomer below it trades programmable modes for a simpler, steady glow, which suits railings and trees where you want one consistent color.

Buy it for a banister, a doorway or a few shrubs. The caveat is that connecting several incandescent sets multiplies heat and wattage, so stay within the maker's limit and avoid wrapping strands around dry decorations such as straw bales.
products.idealFor: Banisters, doorways and shrubs where you want a steady warm color.
products.skipIf: You want animated modes or the longest possible run.

products.name: Joomer Orange Purple Halloween Lights
products.verdict: Orange and purple lights with 8 modes, memory and a timer function.
products.description:
Joomer's orange and purple set offers 8 lighting modes, a memory function and a timer. The timer is the feature that changes how you use string lights: set it once and the display switches on at dusk and off later without you walking to the outlet.

It ranks fourth because the listing gives no length or LED count, so you cannot compare its coverage to the weillsnow or DAZZLE BRIGHT. It earns its place over the TW SHINE below by documenting a timer and memory, which together make nightly use effortless for a porch display.

Buy it if you want to set lights and forget them for the whole of October. The caveat is that without a stated length, you must read the full listing before ordering so you know how many sets your railing or window frame needs.
products.idealFor: Porches and windows where an automatic nightly schedule saves effort.
products.skipIf: You need to compare exact length and LED counts before buying.

products.name: TW SHINE Halloween Lights
products.verdict: A straightforward set with 8 lighting modes and a waterproof, safety-focused build.
products.description:
TW SHINE's Halloween lights offer 8 lighting modes with combination patterns and describe a safe, waterproof build. Combination modes let one strand run steady, twinkle or chase, so the same set can suit a quiet doorway or a lively porch.

It ranks fifth because the listing is thin on the numbers that matter, with no LED count, length or power details in the summary. Compared with the Joomer, which documents memory and a timer, TW SHINE adds weather protection but gives you less control after you switch it off.

Buy it for a covered entry or railing where waterproofing is the main concern. The caveat is that without length or voltage details you should confirm both in the full listing, and keep the power connection off the ground where rain can pool.
products.idealFor: Covered entries and railings where weather resistance matters.
products.skipIf: You want documented length or an automatic timer.

products.name: Runleo Halloween Decorations Pumpkin String Lights Battery Operated
products.verdict: Twenty LED pumpkin-shaped lights on battery power with IP44 splash protection.
products.description:
Runleo's string uses 20 LED pumpkin lights with two lighting modes, battery power and an IP44 waterproof rating. IP44 means the lights resist splashes from any direction, which is enough for a covered porch but not for sitting in standing water.

It ranks last because 20 LEDs is a small display next to the weillsnow's 500, and batteries drain faster than a plugged-in set. Its job is different: it works where no outlet exists, such as a mantel, a wreath, a window sill or a table centerpiece.

Buy it for indoor accents, party tables and spots far from power. The caveat is battery life, which the listing does not quantify, so carry spare batteries and avoid hanging it in a spot that is hard to reach for swapping.
products.idealFor: Mantels, wreaths and tables with no nearby outlet.
products.skipIf: You want to light a roofline or large tree.

whatMatters.detail: Plugs and wire gauge limit how many strands can chain together. Exceed the limit and the far end dims or the fuse blows. DAZZLE BRIGHT states up to three strings under 1000 LEDs. Look for a stated maximum in the listing and add a separate power source before pushing past it. Count the strands before you buy.

Incandescent bulbs, like the 20FT 100Ct set, glow warmer and run hotter, with a higher wattage per foot. LEDs stay cool, use far less power and last longer. For long runs or lights near dry decorations, choose LEDs; for a classic glow on a short strand, incandescent is fine. The bulb type is usually named in the title.

Low-voltage sets such as the weillsnow's 29 volt design use an adapter to step power down, which lowers shock risk around damp outdoor wiring. Look for the voltage in the specifications and a UL listing, and keep adapters off the ground under a cover where rain cannot reach them. Never run a damaged cord outdoors.

Waterproof claims vary. An IP44 rating protects against splashes, while submersion needs a much higher number. Sets without a rating belong under cover. Check the plug and joint seals in the listing, since water usually enters at connectors, not along the wire. Wrap each join in a waterproof cap or tape, and hang connectors facing downward so rain drains off.

Modes change the pattern, memory restores your last choice after a power cut, and a timer switches the lights on and off for you. These matter more over a month than at setup. Look for memory and a timer if the lights stay up all of October. Otherwise you will reset the pattern after every outage.

faq.q: Can I connect different string light sets together?
faq.a: Only if the plugs and voltages match. The weillsnow low-voltage set will not link to the 20FT 100Ct incandescent set. Connect same-model strands only and stay under the stated limit, like DAZZLE BRIGHT's three strings.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with Halloween lights?
faq.a: Running too many strands from one outlet. Chaining past a set's limit dims the far end and overheats plugs. Plan the total LEDs, and use the weillsnow's low-voltage adapter rather than stacking cheap extension cords.

faq.q: Are LED lights worth it over the incandescent 20FT set?
faq.a: For longer runs, yes. LEDs like the weillsnow's 500 stay cool and use little power, while the 20FT 100Ct set glows warmer but draws more per foot and runs hotter near dry decorations.

faq.q: How do I hang string lights outdoors without damage?
faq.a: Use plastic clips or removable hooks instead of staples, which can pierce the wire. Leave slack for wind, and keep the weillsnow or DAZZLE BRIGHT connectors off the ground. Test the strand before you climb.

faq.q: How should I store string lights?
faq.a: Wind them around a piece of cardboard or a reel, keeping the plug end accessible. For the thin weillsnow wire, avoid tight kinks, and take the batteries out of the Runleo set before storage to prevent leakage.

faq.q: Can the battery set stay out in the rain?
faq.a: Light rain, yes. The Runleo string is rated IP44, which resists splashes from any direction. It should not sit in standing water, and its batteries run down faster in cold weather.

finalTake: For a large exterior, buy the weillsnow 500 LED set and enjoy 164 feet on low voltage. Choose DAZZLE BRIGHT 300 LED if you may expand later, and the Runleo pumpkin string for places without an outlet. Skip any set that does not state a connection limit when you plan to chain several together. Measure first, then buy.
